questions.q: Why stream an AI answer instead of waiting for the full response?
options: Users see text after a fraction of a second instead of waiting many seconds
questions.why: Streaming does not change cost or quality; it changes perceived speed.

questions.q: Which ChatClient call returns the answer as it is generated?
questions.why: stream() returns a Flux; content() maps it to the text chunks.

questions.q: What type does stream().content() return?
questions.why: A Reactor Flux that emits each chunk of text.

questions.q: Which media type turns a Flux into Server-Sent Events in a Spring controller?
questions.why: produces = MediaType.TEXT_EVENT_STREAM_VALUE.

questions.q: Your page built with EventSource shows 'Helloworldhowareyou'. Why?
options: SSE strips one leading space after 'data:', so tokens starting with a space lose it
questions.why: Wrap each token in JSON (e.g. a record) so the space survives.

questions.q: What does entity(Candidate.class) do?
options: Saves the answer in a database
Asks the model for JSON matching the record, then maps it to a Candidate
questions.why: BeanOutputConverter adds format instructions with a JSON schema, then deserialises the result.

questions.q: How do you get a List<Candidate> back?
questions.why: Generic types need a ParameterizedTypeReference.

questions.q: What does validateSchema() add?
options: A self-correcting retry when the JSON does not match the schema
questions.why: StructuredOutputValidationAdvisor sends the validation error back to the model and retries (3 attempts by default).

questions.q: What does useProviderStructuredOutput() do?
options: Uses the provider's native JSON-schema mode, when the model supports it
questions.why: Native mode makes the provider return schema-conforming JSON directly. Support varies per model.

questions.q: The model returns yearsOfExperience = 5 for a CV from 2016 to today. Best fix?
options: Extract the raw facts (jobs and years) and compute the total in Java
Ask the model to try harder
questions.why: Structured output guarantees the shape, not the truth. Let the model extract and let code calculate.

questions.q: What is an advisor in Spring AI?
options: An interceptor around the AI call that can change the request and the response
questions.why: Like a servlet filter or AOP around advice, for ChatClient calls.

questions.q: Which interface do you implement for a custom advisor on call()?
questions.why: CallAdvisor.adviseCall(request, chain); StreamAdvisor for stream().

questions.q: Inside adviseCall, how do you continue to the next advisor and the model?
questions.why: Code before nextCall runs on the way in, code after runs on the way out.

questions.q: What decides the order of advisors?
options: getOrder(): lower values run first on the request
questions.why: Advisors implement Ordered.

questions.q: SafeGuardAdvisor finds a sensitive word. What happens?
options: It returns the failure response without calling the model
questions.why: No model call, no tokens spent.

questions.q: Why does a chatbot need chat memory?
options: LLMs are stateless and forget previous messages
questions.why: Memory resends the relevant past messages with each request.

questions.q: Which advisor adds past messages to the prompt?
questions.why: It loads the conversation from ChatMemory before the call and saves the new messages after.

questions.q: What separates Alice's conversation from Bob's?
questions.why: Pass a conversation id per user or per chat.

questions.q: What is the default ChatMemory auto-configured by Spring AI?
options: MessageWindowChatMemory, in memory, keeping the last 20 messages
questions.why: Backed by InMemoryChatMemoryRepository by default.

questions.q: Your bot forgets everything after a restart. What do you add?
questions.why: The in-memory repository lives only as long as the JVM.

questions.q: A 20-second answer feels slow to users. What do you change first?
Which Spring MVC return type streams tokens to the browser?
Your code needs a Java object, not prose. Which method?
With validateSchema() only, every call takes 4x longer and logs 'validation failed'. Likely cause?
options: The model wraps the JSON in markdown code fences, so validation retries
The record has too many fields

questions.q: Which combination gave clean JSON on the first try with Ollama in the lab?
Where should arithmetic like 'total years of experience' happen?
options: In the model, with a higher temperature

questions.q: You want to log the duration and tokens of every AI call. Best tool?
options: A custom CallAdvisor registered with defaultAdvisors

questions.q: Which built-in advisor logs requests and responses at DEBUG level?
Memory is configured, but every user sees the others' context. What is missing?
MessageWindowChatMemory keeps the last N messages. Why not keep everything?
options: Every remembered message is sent again, costing tokens and filling the context window

questions.q: What makes chat memory survive a restart?
Chat memory vs chat history: which statement is true?
options: Memory is what the model needs for context; full history for auditing is stored separately
History is sent to the model, memory is not

challenge.title: Streaming tutor bot with memory
challenge.task: Build a Java tutor bot: GET /tutor/{studentId}/stream?message=... streams the answer, remembers each student's conversation, and POST /tutor/{studentId}/summary returns a StudySummary record (topics covered, weak points, next exercise).
requirements: Stream the chat endpoint as Server-Sent Events, with tokens wrapped in JSON
Use MessageChatMemoryAdvisor with a conversation id per student, persisted with JDBC
Return the summary with entity(StudySummary.class) and validateSchema()
Add a custom advisor that logs duration and total tokens
Block requests containing 'exam answers' with SafeGuardAdvisor
selfCheck: Two students never see each other's context
The tutor still remembers a student after a restart
The summary always deserialises into your record, for 5 different conversations
